data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Amarillis was a nymph who was known for her golden beauty. Her name comes from the Greek word ‘amarysos’, meaning ‘to sparkle’ or ‘to glisten’. In Christianity, Amarillis represents the radiant and golden light of God. The name Amarillis carries the meaning “Golden Glistening” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Amarillis usually hope their child will grow to embody golden glistening and live with faith, good character and purpose.
